franchises.name: Godzilla
franchises.hook: Many continuities, one king
franchises.blurb: Toho’s kaiju series resets more often than it continues. Release order is the clean marathon. Story order keeps each era intact and puts the Monsterverse on its in-universe timeline.
franchises.storyHint: There is no single timeline. Story mode walks each continuity in order — Showa, Heisei, Millennium, the 1998 film, the anime trilogy, Reiwa, then the Monsterverse starting in 1973.

entries.title: Godzilla
entries.note: The original. Everything else is optional after this.

entries.title: All Monsters Attack
entries.note: Largely a clip-show dream story. Easy skip.

entries.title: The Return of Godzilla
entries.note: Reboot. Keeps only the 1954 film.

entries.title: Godzilla 2000: Millennium
entries.note: Another reboot from 1954. Most Millennium films stand alone.

entries.title: Godzilla, Mothra and King Ghidorah
entries.note: GMK. Its own continuity.

entries.title: Godzilla: Tokyo S.O.S.
entries.note: Direct sequel to Against Mechagodzilla.

entries.title: Godzilla
entries.note: Hollywood one-off. Not part of Toho’s numbering.

entries.title: Shin Godzilla
entries.note: Standalone political disaster film.

entries.title: Godzilla: City on the Edge of Battle
Godzilla Minus One
entries.note: Postwar story. Sequel is Minus Zero.

entries.title: Godzilla Minus Zero
entries.note: Sequel set two years after Minus One.

entries.title: Kong: Skull Island
entries.note: Set in 1973. Godzilla is only glimpsed, but it opens the shared universe.

entries.title: Monarch: Legacy of Monsters
entries.note: Splits time between 2015 and the 1950s. Optional before the later films.

entries.title: Godzilla x Kong: The New Empire
Godzilla x Kong: Supernova
entries.note: Scheduled theatrical release.

franchises.name: Star Wars
franchises.hook: Saga films, two orders
franchises.blurb: Release order is how audiences met the galaxy. Story order follows the timeline from the High Republic to the sequel trilogy and slots every animated and live-action series in where it happens.
franchises.storyHint: The Acolyte, then the prequels with The Clone Wars between Episodes II and III, then Solo, Kenobi, Andor and Rebels leading into Rogue One, the original trilogy, the Mandalorian era, and the sequels. Switch the type filter to Films to see just the cinema spine.

entries.title: The Acolyte
entries.note: Set a century before The Phantom Menace. Self-contained.

entries.title: Episode II — Attack of the Clones
The Clone Wars
entries.note: Start with the 2008 film. The war runs between Episodes II and III, with a final season that overlaps Episode III.

entries.title: Episode III — Revenge of the Sith
The Bad Batch
entries.note: Picks up as Episode III ends. Follows The Clone Wars.

entries.title: Obi-Wan Kenobi
entries.note: Set ten years after Episode III.

entries.title: Andor (Season 1)
entries.note: Prequel to Rogue One. Needs no other series.

entries.title: Star Wars Rebels
entries.note: Animated. Runs alongside Andor and sets up Ahsoka.

entries.title: Andor (Season 2)
entries.note: Four time jumps that lead straight into Rogue One.

entries.title: Rogue One
entries.note: Ends minutes before A New Hope.

entries.title: Episode V — The Empire Strikes Back
Episode VI — Return of the Jedi
The Book of Boba Fett
entries.note: Overlaps with The Mandalorian. Watch between seasons 2 and 3.

entries.title: Ahsoka
entries.note: Continues Rebels. Watching Rebels first helps.

entries.title: Skeleton Crew
entries.note: Kids stranded in the same era. Standalone.

entries.title: The Mandalorian and Grogu
entries.note: Follows The Mandalorian season 3.

entries.title: Episode IX — The Rise of Skywalker

franchises.name: Fast & Furious
franchises.hook: Tokyo Drift is out of order
franchises.blurb: The street-racing saga looks linear until you notice Han’s timeline. Story order moves Tokyo Drift to after Fast & Furious 6.
franchises.storyHint: Films 1, 2, 4, 5 and 6, then Tokyo Drift, then Furious 7 onward. Hobbs & Shaw sits between Fate and F9.

entries.title: Tokyo Drift
entries.note: Released third. Story-wise it follows part 6.

entries.title: Hobbs & Shaw
entries.note: Spin-off. Safe to skip.

franchises.name: Alien
franchises.hook: Prequels were made last
franchises.blurb: The crew of the Nostromo came first on screen. Story order starts decades earlier with the Prometheus expedition and the Alien: Earth series.
franchises.storyHint: Prometheus, Covenant and Alien: Earth, then Alien, Romulus, Aliens, Alien 3, and Resurrection.

entries.title: Alien: Earth
entries.note: Set two years before Alien. Standalone, so you can watch it any time.

entries.title: Alien: Romulus
entries.note: Set between Alien and Aliens.

franchises.name: Middle-earth
franchises.hook: Hobbit before the Ring
franchises.blurb: The Lord of the Rings films arrived first and still play best that way. Story order starts centuries earlier with the animated War of the Rohirrim, then Bilbo.
franchises.storyHint: The Rings of Power series, if you want it, then The War of the Rohirrim, the Hobbit trilogy, and The Fellowship, The Two Towers, and The Return of the King.

entries.title: The Rings of Power
entries.note: Amazon’s Second Age series. Same world, separate continuity from the films.

entries.title: The War of the Rohirrim
entries.note: Anime prequel set centuries before The Hobbit.

entries.title: The Hobbit: The Desolation of Smaug
The Hobbit: The Battle of the Five Armies

franchises.name: Jurassic
franchises.hook: Two trilogies, then a restart
franchises.blurb: Park, then World. Release order matches the films. Story order only changes once the animated series are included.
franchises.storyHint: Original trilogy, Jurassic World, Fallen Kingdom, Camp Cretaceous, Dominion, Chaos Theory, then Rebirth.

entries.title: Camp Cretaceous
entries.note: Starts during Jurassic World and runs through the gap before Dominion.

entries.title: Chaos Theory
entries.note: Follows the Camp Cretaceous kids after Dominion.

franchises.name: Marvel Cinematic Universe
franchises.hook: One universe, a timeline of its own
franchises.blurb: Marvel Studios’ films, Disney+ series and specials. Release order is the safest run. Story order follows Marvel’s own timeline, which starts in World War II. The Netflix and ABC shows are not included.
franchises.storyHint: Captain America: The First Avenger and Captain Marvel come first, then the Infinity Saga. Placement of the newer series and the multiverse titles is approximate, because Marvel itself keeps adjusting it.

entries.title: Eyes of Wakanda
entries.note: Animated. Follows Wakandan guardians across history.

entries.title: Captain Marvel
entries.note: Set in 1995, long before it was released.

entries.title: Iron Man
entries.note: Where the release-order run begins.

entries.title: Your Friendly Neighborhood Spider-Man
entries.note: Animated. Early days of Peter Parker as Spider-Man.

entries.title: Black Widow
entries.note: Set just after Civil War, released after Endgame.

entries.title: Avengers: Endgame
entries.note: Closes the Infinity Saga.

entries.title: Loki
entries.note: Two seasons. Opens the multiverse, so watch it before the later films.

entries.title: The Falcon and the Winter Soldier
Shang-Chi and the Legend of the Ten Rings
Doctor Strange in the Multiverse of Madness
entries.note: Watch WandaVision and No Way Home first.

entries.title: Werewolf by Night
entries.note: A short black-and-white special. Standalone.

entries.title: The Guardians of the Galaxy Holiday Special
entries.note: Light and festive. Skippable.

entries.title: Agatha All Along
entries.note: Follows WandaVision.

entries.title: Daredevil: Born Again (Season 1)
entries.note: Helps to have seen the Netflix Daredevil seasons, but not required.

entries.title: The Punisher: One Last Kill
entries.note: A one-off special that follows Daredevil: Born Again.

entries.title: VisionQuest
entries.note: Continues Vision’s story after WandaVision.

entries.title: Avengers: Doomsday
entries.note: Scheduled theatrical release.

entries.title: Avengers: Secret Wars
entries.note: Scheduled theatrical release.

entries.title: The Fantastic Four: First Steps
entries.note: Set on a different Earth. Its heroes cross over later.

entries.title: X-Men ’97
entries.note: Animated revival of the 1990s cartoon.

entries.title: What If…?
entries.note: Animated anthology of alternate realities. Three seasons.

entries.title: Marvel Zombies
entries.note: Animated horror spin-off from What If…?.

franchises.name: Star Trek
franchises.hook: Sixty years of sequels and prequels
franchises.blurb: Release order is a tour through the decades. Story order runs from the 22nd century to the 32nd, with the alternate Kelvin timeline kept apart so it cannot tangle the main sequence.
franchises.storyHint: Enterprise, Discovery seasons 1–2 and Strange New Worlds, then the original series and its films, the 24th-century shows and films, the Kelvin timeline, and finally the 32nd century. The 24th-century shows overlap each other and the films, so each is placed whole.

entries.title: Star Trek: Strange New Worlds
entries.note: Leads straight into the original series. Four seasons so far.

entries.title: Star Trek: The Animated Series
entries.note: Animated follow-up to the original series.

entries.title: Star Trek II: The Wrath of Khan
Star Trek III: The Search for Spock
Star Trek IV: The Voyage Home
Star Trek V: The Final Frontier
Star Trek VI: The Undiscovered Country
Star Trek: Section 31
entries.note: Streaming film set in 2324. Standalone.

entries.title: Star Trek: Deep Space Nine
entries.note: Starts while The Next Generation is still running.

entries.title: Star Trek: Generations
entries.note: Hands the films from the original crew to the Next Generation crew.

entries.title: Star Trek: Lower Decks
entries.note: Animated comedy. Works best after The Next Generation.

entries.title: Star Trek: Picard
entries.note: Best after The Next Generation and Voyager.

entries.title: Star Trek: Discovery (Seasons 3–5)
entries.note: The crew jumps nine centuries into the future.

entries.title: Star Trek
entries.note: Alternate timeline reboot. Needs no earlier Trek.

franchises.name: X-Men
franchises.hook: A timeline that rewrites itself
franchises.blurb: Fox’s mutant films were never planned as one story. Release order is how the tangle formed. Story order follows the set years, so the 1960s prequel comes first.
franchises.storyHint: First Class, Origins: Wolverine, Days of Future Past, Apocalypse and Dark Phoenix, then the original trilogy, then The Wolverine, Deadpool, and Logan. Deadpool & Wolverine belongs to the Marvel Cinematic Universe list.

entries.title: X-Men: First Class
entries.note: Set in 1962.

entries.title: X-Men Origins: Wolverine
entries.note: Widely considered skippable.

entries.title: X-Men: Days of Future Past
entries.note: Rewrites the timeline. Later films follow the new version.

entries.title: X-Men: Apocalypse
entries.note: Set in 1983.

entries.title: Dark Phoenix
entries.note: Set in 1992.

entries.title: The Wolverine
entries.note: Set after The Last Stand.

entries.title: The New Mutants
entries.note: Standalone teen horror spin-off.

entries.title: Logan
entries.note: Set in 2029. The farewell for this version of the X-Men.

franchises.name: DC Films & Shows
franchises.hook: Two universes, one reboot
franchises.blurb: The DC Extended Universe ran from 2013 to 2023, then DC Studios started over with a new DC Universe. Release order shows how the first gave way to the second. Story order keeps each universe together.
franchises.storyHint: The DC Extended Universe first, with Wonder Woman’s two films moved to their own decades, then the new DC Universe in release order.

entries.title: Wonder Woman
entries.note: Set in 1918.

entries.title: Batman v Superman: Dawn of Justice
Justice League
entries.note: Theatrical cut. Skip it if you watch the Snyder Cut.

entries.title: Peacemaker (Season 1)
entries.note: Follows The Suicide Squad.

entries.title: The Flash
entries.note: Resets part of the timeline.

entries.title: Aquaman and the Lost Kingdom
entries.note: Last film of the DC Extended Universe.

entries.title: Creature Commandos
entries.note: Animated. First title of the new DC Universe.

entries.title: Peacemaker (Season 2)
entries.note: Moves the character into the new DC Universe.

entries.title: Man of Tomorrow
entries.note: Scheduled theatrical release.

franchises.name: Wizarding World
franchises.hook: The prequels come first in the story
franchises.blurb: Harry Potter first, Fantastic Beasts later, is how audiences saw it. Story order puts Newt Scamander’s 1920s films before Hogwarts. HBO’s new Harry Potter series is a fresh adaptation, not a sequel.
franchises.storyHint: The three Fantastic Beasts films, then the eight Harry Potter films. HBO’s reboot comes last.

entries.title: Fantastic Beasts and Where to Find Them
entries.note: Set in 1926.

entries.title: Fantastic Beasts: The Crimes of Grindelwald
Fantastic Beasts: The Secrets of Dumbledore
Harry Potter and the Philosopher’s Stone
Harry Potter and the Chamber of Secrets
Harry Potter and the Prisoner of Azkaban
Harry Potter and the Goblet of Fire
Harry Potter and the Order of the Phoenix
Harry Potter and the Half-Blood Prince
Harry Potter and the Deathly Hallows — Part 1
Harry Potter and the Deathly Hallows — Part 2
Harry Potter (HBO series)
entries.note: A new adaptation that starts again from the first book. Scheduled release.

franchises.name: The Conjuring Universe
franchises.hook: Released out of order on purpose
franchises.blurb: The horror films were made in whatever order they were green-lit, so release order jumps between decades. Story order runs from 1952 to 1986 and makes the cases read as one long haunting.
franchises.storyHint: The Nun, Annabelle: Creation, The Nun II, Annabelle, The Conjuring, Annabelle Comes Home, The Curse of La Llorona, The Conjuring 2, The Devil Made Me Do It, then Last Rites.

entries.title: The Nun
entries.note: Set in 1952.

entries.title: Annabelle: Creation
entries.note: Set in 1955.

entries.title: The Nun II
entries.note: Set in 1956.

entries.title: Annabelle
entries.note: Set in 1967.

entries.title: The Conjuring
entries.note: Set in 1971.

entries.title: Annabelle Comes Home
entries.note: Set in 1972.

entries.title: The Curse of La Llorona
entries.note: Set in 1973. Only loosely connected.

entries.title: The Conjuring 2
entries.note: Set in 1977.

entries.title: The Conjuring: The Devil Made Me Do It
entries.note: Set in 1981.

entries.title: The Conjuring: Last Rites
entries.note: Set in 1986.

franchises.name: Halloween
franchises.hook: Five continuities, one mask
franchises.blurb: Nearly every sequel pretends some of the earlier ones never happened. Release order is the history. Story order keeps each continuity together so you can pick one path through them.
franchises.storyHint: The 1978 original and Halloween II are shared. Then choose a path: the Thorn cult films, the H20 pair, the 2018 trilogy, or Rob Zombie’s remakes. Halloween III is a standalone.

entries.title: Halloween
entries.note: The start of every continuity.

entries.title: Halloween II
entries.note: Picks up the same night. The H20 films and the 2018 trilogy handle it differently.

entries.title: Halloween III: Season of the Witch
entries.note: No Michael Myers. Its own story.

entries.title: Halloween 4: The Return of Michael Myers
Halloween 5: The Revenge of Michael Myers
Halloween: The Curse of Michael Myers
Halloween H20: 20 Years Later
entries.note: Follows the first two films and ignores 4 to 6.

entries.title: Halloween
entries.note: A direct sequel to the 1978 film. Ignores everything else.

entries.title: Halloween (2007)
entries.note: Rob Zombie’s remake.

franchises.name: Terminator
franchises.hook: Each sequel picks its own timeline
franchises.blurb: After Judgment Day, every new film or show chose which earlier ones still count. Release order is how they appeared. Story order walks each branch in turn.
franchises.storyHint: The first two films and Dark Fate form the core branch. The Sarah Connor Chronicles, the T3 branch, Genisys and Terminator Zero each go their own way.

entries.title: Terminator: Dark Fate
entries.note: Direct sequel to Terminator 2. Ignores films 3 to 5.

entries.title: Terminator: The Sarah Connor Chronicles
entries.note: Follows Terminator 2 and ignores Terminator 3.

entries.title: Terminator Genisys
entries.note: A reboot that rewrites the first film. Widely considered skippable.

entries.title: Terminator Zero
entries.note: Animated Netflix series in its own continuity.

franchises.name: Transformers
franchises.hook: The prequels came later
franchises.blurb: The live-action series began with Michael Bay in 2007, then looked backward. Story order starts on Cybertron and runs through the 1980s and 1990s before reaching the original film.
franchises.storyHint: Transformers One, Bumblebee, Rise of the Beasts, then the five Bay films.

entries.title: Transformers One
entries.note: Animated origin story of Optimus Prime and Megatron.

entries.title: Bumblebee
entries.note: Set in 1987.

entries.title: Transformers: Rise of the Beasts
entries.note: Set in 1994. A sequel to Bumblebee.

franchises.name: Predator
franchises.hook: The hunt starts centuries earlier
franchises.blurb: The newest films reach back to 1719 and forward to the far future. Story order starts with Prey and runs through the crossovers to Badlands.
franchises.storyHint: Prey and Killer of Killers, then the modern-day films from Predator to The Predator, then Badlands in the far future.

entries.title: Prey
entries.note: Set in 1719.

entries.title: Predator: Killer of Killers
entries.note: Animated anthology across three eras of history.

entries.title: Predator 2
entries.note: Set in 1997.

entries.title: Alien vs. Predator
entries.note: Crossover with the Alien films. Standalone.

entries.title: Aliens vs. Predator: Requiem
entries.note: Direct sequel to the first crossover.

entries.title: Predator: Badlands
entries.note: Set in the far future, in the same universe as the Alien films.

franchises.name: Mad Max
franchises.hook: The prequel comes last
franchises.blurb: Fury Road looked like a sequel in 2015 and Furiosa then went back to tell her story. Story order puts the prequel just before Fury Road.
franchises.storyHint: The original trilogy, then Furiosa, then Fury Road.

entries.title: Furiosa: A Mad Max Saga
entries.note: Prequel to Fury Road. Spans about fifteen years.

franchises.name: Indiana Jones
franchises.hook: The second film is really the first
franchises.blurb: Temple of Doom is a prequel to Raiders of the Lost Ark. Story order puts it first and optionally begins with the television series about the young Indy.
franchises.storyHint: The Young Indiana Jones Chronicles, then Temple of Doom, Raiders, The Last Crusade, Kingdom of the Crystal Skull, and Dial of Destiny.

entries.title: The Young Indiana Jones Chronicles
entries.note: Follows Indy from childhood. Not needed for the films.

entries.title: Indiana Jones and the Temple of Doom
entries.note: Set in 1935, a year before Raiders.

entries.title: Raiders of the Lost Ark
entries.note: Set in 1936.

entries.title: Indiana Jones and the Last Crusade
Indiana Jones and the Kingdom of the Crystal Skull
Indiana Jones and the Dial of Destiny

franchises.name: The Hunger Games
franchises.hook: Two prequels, decades earlier
franchises.blurb: Katniss’s story came first. The prequels follow earlier Games, so story order starts decades before the first film.
franchises.storyHint: The Ballad of Songbirds & Snakes, then Sunrise on the Reaping, then the four original films.

entries.title: The Ballad of Songbirds & Snakes
entries.note: Set 64 years before the first film.

entries.title: Sunrise on the Reaping
entries.note: Set 24 years before the first film. Scheduled release.

franchises.name: Dune
franchises.hook: A prequel set 10,000 years earlier
franchises.blurb: Denis Villeneuve’s films tell the story of Paul Atreides. HBO’s Dune: Prophecy goes ten millennia back, so story order starts there.
franchises.storyHint: Dune: Prophecy, then Dune, Part Two, and Part Three.

entries.title: Dune: Prophecy
entries.note: Set 10,000 years before the films. Not needed for them.

entries.title: Dune: Part Three
entries.note: Scheduled theatrical release.

franchises.name: James Bond
franchises.hook: Twenty-five Eon films, one man, loose continuity
franchises.blurb: The Eon series ran from 1962 to 2021 and rebooted itself twice, so there is no single story order. Watch it in release order and you get every era, every Bond and every gadget in the order audiences met them.
franchises.storyHint: Release order is the honest answer. The two non-Eon films are optional and sit outside the series.

entries.title: Casino Royale
entries.note: A 1967 comedy parody, unrelated to the Eon series.

entries.title: The Man with the Golden Gun
Never Say Never Again
entries.note: A remake of Thunderball made outside Eon, with Sean Connery back as Bond.

entries.title: Casino Royale
entries.note: The first Craig film and a hard reboot of the series.

entries.title: Quantum of Solace
entries.note: Picks up minutes after Casino Royale ends.

franchises.name: Mission: Impossible
franchises.hook: Eight films, one increasingly impossible stunt
franchises.blurb: The film series rebooted the 1960s show with Ethan Hunt and has kept a single loose continuity ever since. Each film hands the director a new style, so release order is the only order that makes sense.
franchises.storyHint: Release order. Dead Reckoning and The Final Reckoning are one story split in two.

entries.title: Mission: Impossible – Fallout
entries.note: Direct follow-on from Rogue Nation.

entries.title: Mission: Impossible – Dead Reckoning Part One
Mission: Impossible – The Final Reckoning
entries.note: Second half of the Dead Reckoning story.

franchises.name: John Wick
franchises.hook: A hitman, a dog, and a very expensive suit
franchises.blurb: Four films, one prequel series and one spin-off, all built on the same hotel-for-assassins mythology. Story order puts the 1970s Continental series first, then the films, with Ballerina tucked between Chapters 3 and 4.
franchises.storyHint: The Continental is a 1970s prequel; Ballerina runs alongside Chapter 3 and ends before Chapter 4.

entries.title: The Continental
entries.note: A three-part prequel set in 1975. Optional, but it explains the hotel.

entries.title: Ballerina
entries.note: Set during the events of Chapter 3.

franchises.name: The Matrix
franchises.hook: Follow the white rabbit, then the sequels
franchises.blurb: The 1999 original, two sequels released six months apart, an animated anthology that fills in the world, and a 2021 epilogue. The Animatrix sits between the first two films.
franchises.storyHint: The Matrix, The Animatrix, Reloaded, Revolutions, then Resurrections twenty years later.

entries.title: The Animatrix
entries.note: Nine animated shorts that set up the world and the war. Watch after the first film.

franchises.name: Back to the Future
franchises.hook: Three films, one DeLorean, no reboots
franchises.blurb: A single tight trilogy about the same afternoon in 1985 going wrong in three directions, plus an animated series that continues after Part III. Release order is story order.
franchises.storyHint: Parts I, II and III in order. The animated series is optional and runs after the trilogy.

entries.title: Back to the Future Part II
Back to the Future Part III
Back to the Future: The Animated Series

franchises.name: Pirates of the Caribbean
franchises.hook: Five films, one curse, a lot of rum
franchises.blurb: The first three films are one continuous story; the last two are stand-alone adventures with the same crew. Release order keeps the trilogy intact.
franchises.storyHint: Release order. Dead Men Tell No Tales brings back characters from the trilogy.

entries.title: Pirates of the Caribbean: The Curse of the Black Pearl
Pirates of the Caribbean: Dead Man's Chest
Pirates of the Caribbean: At World's End
Pirates of the Caribbean: On Stranger Tides
Pirates of the Caribbean: Dead Men Tell No Tales

franchises.name: Planet of the Apes
franchises.hook: Three separate timelines about the same planet
franchises.blurb: The 1968 original and its four sequels, Tim Burton's 2001 remake, and the modern Caesar trilogy that leads into Kingdom. They are three different continuities, so pick one lane and stay in it.
franchises.storyHint: Caesar timeline: Rise, Dawn, War, Kingdom. Original timeline: Planet, Beneath, Escape, Conquest, Battle. The 2001 remake stands alone.

entries.title: Beneath the Planet of the Apes
Escape from the Planet of the Apes
Conquest of the Planet of the Apes
Battle for the Planet of the Apes
Planet of the Apes
entries.note: Tim Burton's remake. Its own continuity, safe to skip.

entries.title: Rise of the Planet of the Apes
Dawn of the Planet of the Apes
War for the Planet of the Apes
Kingdom of the Planet of the Apes
entries.note: Set generations after War.

franchises.name: Rocky & Creed
franchises.hook: Nine films, one staircase
franchises.blurb: Rocky ran from 1976 to 2006, then handed the gloves to Adonis Creed in 2015. It is one continuous story, so release order is story order.
franchises.storyHint: Rocky I–V, Rocky Balboa, then Creed, Creed II and Creed III.

entries.title: Rocky Balboa
entries.note: Ignores most of Rocky V and closes the original run.

entries.title: Creed II
entries.note: Brings back Ivan Drago from Rocky IV.

entries.title: Creed III
entries.note: The first film without Rocky.

franchises.name: Die Hard
franchises.hook: One man, five very bad days
franchises.blurb: The 1988 original invented a genre and the sequels keep finding new buildings for John McClane to wreck. Each film stands alone; release order is enough.
franchises.storyHint: Release order. Only the first two are closely linked.

entries.title: A Good Day to Die Hard

franchises.name: Ghostbusters
franchises.hook: Two timelines, four proton packs
franchises.blurb: The 1984 original and its 1989 sequel, a 2016 reboot that ignores both, then Afterlife and Frozen Empire which return to the original story. Watch the original two first or Afterlife will not land.
franchises.storyHint: Ghostbusters, Ghostbusters II, Afterlife, Frozen Empire. The 2016 film is a separate reboot.

entries.title: Ghostbusters
entries.note: A standalone reboot with a new cast. Nothing later depends on it.

franchises.name: Men in Black
franchises.hook: Four films, one neuralyzer
franchises.blurb: A comic-book adaptation that turned into a trilogy about agents K and J, plus a 2019 spin-off with a different pair. Light, episodic and easy to watch in release order.
franchises.storyHint: Release order. Men in Black 3 involves time travel but is seen after the second film.

entries.title: Men in Black: International
entries.note: A spin-off with new leads, set in the same world.

franchises.name: Toy Story
franchises.hook: Five films, one toy chest
franchises.blurb: Pixar's first film and still its most reliable series. Each entry stands alone but the endings build on each other, so release order gets the emotional payoff.
franchises.storyHint: Release order, all five films.

franchises.name: Shrek
franchises.hook: Four films and two Puss in Boots side stories
franchises.blurb: DreamWorks' fairy-tale spoof, plus the Puss in Boots spin-offs. The first Puss film is a prequel; The Last Wish is set after the main series.
franchises.storyHint: Shrek, Shrek 2, Shrek the Third, Shrek Forever After, then the two Puss in Boots films.

entries.title: Puss in Boots
entries.note: A prequel, so it can also be watched first.

entries.title: Puss in Boots: The Last Wish

franchises.name: Sonic the Hedgehog
franchises.hook: Three films and a Knuckles series
franchises.blurb: The film series that started as a joke and became a solid family action trilogy. Knuckles sits between the second and third films and explains where he went.
franchises.storyHint: Sonic, Sonic 2, Knuckles, then Sonic 3.

entries.title: Knuckles
entries.note: Six episodes set between Sonic 2 and Sonic 3.

franchises.name: Avatar
franchises.hook: One story, told in four instalments
franchises.blurb: James Cameron's Pandora films are one continuous story with years between chapters. The 2009 original, The Way of Water, then Fire and Ash.
franchises.storyHint: Release order. Each film picks up shortly after the last.

franchises.name: The Twilight Saga
franchises.hook: Five films, one love triangle
franchises.blurb: Four novels adapted into five films, with the last book split in two. Straight release order, and the books are a genuinely different experience from the films.
franchises.storyHint: Twilight, New Moon, Eclipse, Breaking Dawn Parts 1 and 2.

entries.title: The Twilight Saga: Breaking Dawn – Part 1
The Twilight Saga: Breaking Dawn – Part 2

franchises.name: Jason Bourne
franchises.hook: Five films, one lost identity
franchises.blurb: The Ludlum novels became a trilogy about amnesia and surveillance, then a spin-off and a reunion. Legacy runs alongside Ultimatum rather than after it.
franchises.storyHint: Identity, Supremacy, Ultimatum, Jason Bourne. Legacy happens at the same time as Ultimatum.

entries.title: The Bourne Legacy
entries.note: Set during Ultimatum with a new lead.

franchises.name: Scream
franchises.hook: Seven films, one small town, one mask
franchises.blurb: Wes Craven's slasher series kept reinventing itself: a trilogy, a fourth film, then a new generation in 2022. Release order is the only order that lets the jokes and the rules land.
franchises.storyHint: Release order. The 2022 film is a sequel, not a remake, and Scream VI picks it up directly.

entries.title: Scream (2022)
entries.note: A new cast, the same Woodsboro history.

entries.title: Scream VI
entries.note: Moves the survivors to New York.

franchises.name: Final Destination
franchises.hook: Death has a design, and it does not skip
franchises.blurb: Six films built on one idea: a premonition saves a group, then death works through them in order. The set pieces are the point, so release order keeps the escalation intact.
franchises.storyHint: Release order. Bloodlines follows the granddaughter of the first film's survivor.

entries.title: Final Destination 5
entries.note: Ends by looping back to the first film.

franchises.name: Saw
franchises.hook: Ten films, one puppet, a very complicated timeline
franchises.blurb: The series ran forwards for seven films, then started filling in its own history. Story order puts Saw X between the first two films and leaves the two spin-offs for last.
franchises.storyHint: Saw, Saw X, then Saw II to Saw 3D. Jigsaw and Spiral follow the main run; Spiral is a separate story.

entries.title: Saw IV
entries.note: Runs alongside Saw III.

entries.title: Jigsaw
entries.note: A later sequel that revisits the original traps.

entries.title: Spiral
entries.note: A spin-off with a new cast, set outside the main Jigsaw story.

entries.title: Saw X
entries.note: Set between Saw and Saw II.

franchises.name: Rambo
franchises.hook: One soldier, five films, four decades
franchises.blurb: First Blood was a small film about a veteran who will not be pushed around. The sequels turned John Rambo into a one-man war, and Last Blood brought him home.
franchises.storyHint: Release order. First Blood is the quiet one; the rest get louder.

franchises.name: The Godfather
franchises.hook: Three films about one family business
franchises.blurb: Mario Puzo's Corleones, filmed by Coppola as a trilogy that moves between the 1900s and the 1980s. Part II cuts between Vito's rise and Michael's fall, but release order is still the clearest way in.
franchises.storyHint: Release order. Part II's flashbacks fill in Vito's history without needing to be watched first.

entries.title: The Godfather Part III
entries.note: A 2020 recut, The Godfather Coda, is an alternate edit of this film.

franchises.name: Underworld
franchises.hook: Vampires, werewolves, and a very old feud
franchises.blurb: Five films about the war between the vampires and the Lycans. Rise of the Lycans is a medieval prequel; the other four run in release order.
franchises.storyHint: Rise of the Lycans first, then Underworld, Evolution, Awakening and Blood Wars.

entries.title: Underworld: Rise of the Lycans
entries.note: A prequel set centuries before the first film.

franchises.name: The Last of Us
franchises.hook: Two games, one long walk across America
franchises.blurb: Naughty Dog's post-outbreak story is told in two games and one prequel chapter. Play the first game, its Left Behind chapter, then Part II; the emotional order matters more here than in most series.
franchises.storyHint: The Last of Us, Left Behind, then The Last of Us Part II.

entries.title: The Last of Us: Left Behind
entries.note: A two-part prequel chapter, best played after the first game.

entries.title: The Last of Us Part II

franchises.name: Uncharted
franchises.hook: Six adventures, one very unlucky treasure hunter
franchises.blurb: Naughty Dog's treasure-hunting series runs on set pieces, but the relationships build across the games. Golden Abyss is a Vita prequel, and The Lost Legacy hands the lead to Chloe.
franchises.storyHint: Golden Abyss is optional and comes first; then Drake's Fortune through A Thief's End, then The Lost Legacy.

entries.title: Uncharted: Golden Abyss
entries.note: A Vita prequel set before Drake's Fortune.

entries.title: Uncharted: The Lost Legacy
entries.note: A standalone story with Chloe and Nadine.

franchises.name: God of War
franchises.hook: Two mythologies, eight games, one angry father
franchises.blurb: The Greek games tell Kratos's origin out of order: Ascension and Chains of Olympus are prequels, and Ghost of Sparta sits between the first two main games. The 2018 game starts a Norse chapter with his son.
franchises.storyHint: Greek story order first: Ascension, Chains of Olympus, God of War, Ghost of Sparta, God of War II, God of War III. Then God of War (2018) and Ragnarök.

entries.title: God of War: Chains of Olympus
entries.note: A prequel set ten years before the first game.

entries.title: God of War: Ghost of Sparta
entries.note: Set between the first game and God of War II.

entries.title: God of War: Ascension
entries.note: A prequel set before Kratos's servitude to Ares.

entries.title: God of War (2018)
entries.note: A soft reboot that moves the story to Norse mythology.

franchises.name: Mass Effect
franchises.hook: One commander, one crew, one galaxy
franchises.blurb: BioWare's space opera is built on choices that carry between games, so the trilogy wants to be played in order with one save. Andromeda is a separate story in another galaxy.
franchises.storyHint: Mass Effect, Mass Effect 2, Mass Effect 3. Andromeda is a distant spin-off and can be played any time after.

entries.title: Mass Effect 2
entries.note: Imports your choices and your Shepard from the first game.

entries.title: Mass Effect: Andromeda
entries.note: A separate story, set in another galaxy.

franchises.name: Halo
franchises.hook: Eight games, one long war with the Covenant
franchises.blurb: The Master Chief games jump around their own timeline: Reach is a prequel, and ODST runs alongside Halo 2. Story order starts at the fall of Reach and ends with Infinite.
franchises.storyHint: Reach, Combat Evolved, Halo 2, ODST, Halo 3, Halo 4, Halo 5, then Infinite.

entries.title: Halo 3: ODST
entries.note: Runs alongside Halo 2 and ends before Halo 3.

entries.title: Halo: Reach
entries.note: A prequel that ends where Halo: Combat Evolved begins.

franchises.name: The Witcher
franchises.hook: Three games, two expansions, one witcher
franchises.blurb: CD Projekt's games continue Andrzej Sapkowski's books rather than adapting them. The two Witcher 3 expansions are self-contained stories that sit after the main game.
franchises.storyHint: The Witcher, The Witcher 2, The Witcher 3, then Hearts of Stone and Blood and Wine.

entries.title: The Witcher 3: Hearts of Stone
entries.note: An expansion for The Witcher 3.

entries.title: The Witcher 3: Blood and Wine
entries.note: The final expansion, set in Toussaint.
